newsitem.title: USA: Japan seen comfortable with dlr/yen range 105-115.
newsitem.headline: Japan seen comfortable with dlr/yen range 105-115.

text.p: President of Citicorp/Citibank Japan Masamoto Yashiro said a dollar range between 105 and 115 yen would likely satisfy most parties in Japan.
In response to a Reuter query, Yashiro said that range is probably "politically and economically acceptable." He spoke to Reuters after addressing a Columbia Business School conference here.
Furthermore, Yashiro said that dollar range may not only be acceptable but also "comfortable."
He noted that some Japanese industries have moved their production centers overseas. If the yen weakens too much, then moving their imports into Japan becomes very expensive.
Therefore, he concluded the dollar range between 105 to 115 yen is probably acceptable to both importers and exporters in Japan.
As for the Japanese government's latest deregulation package dubbed "The Big Bang," Yashiro offered both praise and criticism.
The plan should raise Tokyo's profile as an international business center by increasing foreign participation in Japanese financial markets by aggressive foreign institutions.
But Yashiro complained the package did nothing to bring real competition to the Japanese financial sector.
Without true competition, financial institutions fail to evolve into more viable, efficient entities, Yashiro said.
"If you let them really compete among themselves, ... then only the efficient ones survive," said Yashiro, who is also an executive vice president of Citicorp/Citibank, N.A.

Yashiro's comments on the dollar/yen rate came a month after Ford Motor Co vice president David McCammon told Reuters Financial Television the U.S. automaker is also assuming a dollar-yen range of 105 to 115 in its planning for the coming year. However, McCammon said "this yen-relationship really doesn't make sense and gives the Japanese some sort of advantage."
